name: Content Placeholder 2
text: Given the growing volume of online internship postings, candidates currently have no reliable, data-driven way to determine whether a posting is genuinely worth pursuing, this project aims to design an NLP-based system that analyzes job role, company, location, and compensation signals to generate an interpretable "worth score" for internship postings.

name: Content Placeholder 2
text:
InternWorth is an NLP-driven composite scoring system that evaluates internship postings from the candidate's perspective, producing an interpretable Worth Score broken into transparent sub-scores.
Combines rule-based extraction, Named Entity Recognition, sentiment analysis, and transformer-based classification across six independent signal categories, aggregated into one explainable output.
Unlike existing job-posting NLP research focus on fraud detection or employer-side matching, InternWorth targets candidate-side value assessment, a distinct and underexplored problem.

name: Content Placeholder 2
text:
Online internship marketplaces have grown rapidly, but they have introduced a new problem: information asymmetry.
A posting may look attractive (big brand, catchy title) while offering little real compensation or learning value.
A lesser-known company's posting may in fact offer excellent mentorship, fair pay, and real conversion potential.
Manually cross-referencing pay, reputation, and legitimacy across platforms is not realistic for most students, InternWorth automates this using NLP, with a transparent breakdown of the reasoning behind each score.

name: Content Placeholder 2
text:
Fraud / Scam Detection: Binary real-vs-fake classifiers (TF-IDF + ensembles) trained on the Kaggle Fake Job Postings dataset assumes the job is fake, says nothing about a real job's value.
Resume Job Matching: Optimizes candidate-to-role (embedding similarity + skill-graph matching) fit via skill extraction tells you if you qualify, not whether the job is worth taking.
Manual Research: Reading scattered reviews and asking seniors time-consuming, inconsistent, and inaccessible to most students.

name: Content Placeholder 2
text:
InternWorth shifts the question from “is this intern fake?” to “is this intern worth my time?”
Multi-signal, not single-label: Six independent extraction modules (NER + sentiment analysis + rule-based pattern matching) instead of one binary classifier.
Explainable by design: Full sub-score breakdown shown alongside the aggregate score - never a black box (weighted multi-factor scoring, not a single black-box label).
Candidate-side focus: Optimizes for the applicant's real outcome (compensation fairness, role clarity, legitimacy), not employer- or fraud-side signals.
Grounded in labor policy: Weights informed by fairness reasoning pay and red flags weighted heaviest.

name: Content Placeholder 2
text:
Data Ingestion: Postings and supporting data (reviews, cost-of-living index) are collected from Internshala, LinkedIn, and Naukri.
Preprocessing: Text is cleaned and normalized; Named Entity Recognition extracts structured fields like pay, location, and company name.
Six Parallel Modules: Each of the six signal categories is scored independently, so no single module can dominate the outcome.
Aggregation Engine: Sub-scores are combined via a weighted sum into the final InternWorth Score, shown with its full breakdown.

Explainable multi-signal design: six sub-scores, not one black-box label. Directly aligned with SDG 8 (Decent Work) and SDG 4 (Quality Education). Feasible scope for a single-semester coursework implementation.
